title: meta-os.config.json — instance estate configuration
description: Schema for a meta-os instance's estate config (meta-os.config.json): the estate knowledge an adopter declares — variable prefixes, backlog mirrors, and memory topology. This is the FRAMEWORK level: valid keys, valid enum values, and defaults, carrying ZERO values. Deployment concerns (instanceRoot, frameworkRoot, github.*, auth, corsOrigins, claudeHome, dataDir) live in the dashboard's instance.config.json, not here. Every key is optional; omitting the file yields default behaviour. The `instance` block is the one key the framework writes (at bootstrap) rather than the adopter.

instance.description: The instantiation record scripts/bootstrap.sh writes on first run (one-repository layout, systems/distribution.md). name: the instance's name. bootstrapped: the date of the first run, YYYY-MM-DD. template: the framework commit whose instance-template/ was copied in; scripts/upgrade.sh diffs instance-template/ from it to report what the template changed since, and --ack-template moves it forward once the operator has reviewed that diff.

publicRepoGate.description: The instance's settings for scripts/public_repo_gate.py: what counts as instance data in a public repository. Every key is optional; omitted, the framework's key shape and home-path check apply.

keyPattern.description: Regex matching this instance's tracker keys; replaces the framework's generic key shape.

allowedTokens.description: Exact tokens that match the key pattern and are not keys, added to the framework's allow-list.

exemptRepos.description: OWNER/NAME of public repositories whose text carries tracker keys by design; machine paths are still checked there.

pathPrefixes.description: Absolute path prefixes that are instance data, besides any home path.

swarm.description: The autonomous pipeline's bounds, cadence and identities (systems/pipeline.md). The loop reads these and never writes them; prompts and repository routing stay in the pipeline's own configuration file. Every key is optional; omitted, the default applies.

lanes.description: m_max: the lane slots. The sizing rule gives 5; a proof of concept uses 3.

min_lanes.description: m_min: the fewest working lanes the regulator keeps while the pipe runs.

tokens.description: N: the CONWIP cap, items from start until DONE or NO GO. Set by a human from the sizing; default twice `lanes`.

fairness_share.description: The largest share of the tokens one space may hold.

automerge_classes.description: Change classes that merge without the human station.

review_sla_days.description: The review-age limit: a space whose oldest item in review is older takes no new work.

review_queue_cap.description: The most items one space may hold in review before it takes no new work.

lane_budget.description: A run's cap, as a multiple of its expected cost; over it the run is interrupted and given back.

max_retries.description: How many times an item may be given back before it is no longer admissible.

tick_minutes.description: The tick interval; an early tick follows a run's end or a control.

reserves.description: The fraction of each usage window's allowance never spent.

mileage_ticks.description: The span, in ticks, of the per-window mileage average.

stale_after_ticks.description: Ticks without any session activity before a lane is stale and reaped.

max_stale_reaps.description: Reaps of the same item before it is held for a human.

stall_after_ticks.description: Ticks with every lane idle while admissible work exists before a stall is reported.

executable_spaces.description: The spaces whose items the pipeline may start. Empty: none.

record_repository.description: The private repository the loop writes its state, plans, results and events to; never the framework, never a place for secrets.

path.description: The local clone the loop writes and a local dashboard reads.

adapter.description: `command` runs the configured command and falls back to reasoning on failure; `reasoning` orders the admissible set itself.

command.description: The planner command and its arguments, for the `command` adapter.

repair_max_items.description: A change touching at most this many items, or one lane, is repaired rather than solved cold.

churn_cap.description: A repair whose edit distance exceeds this is discarded for a cold solve.

cold_every_hours.description: Hours between scheduled cold solves; one also runs at window start.

repair_timeout_seconds.description: Time allowed for a repair before the tick plans by reasoning.

cold_timeout_seconds.description: Time allowed for a cold solve before the tick plans by reasoning.

dashboard_controls.description: Render the Pipeline tab's controls on a dashboard reading a local source. A hosted or GitHub-sourced dashboard never offers them.

visibility_probe.description: Probe each run's repository through scripts/public_repo_gate.py; one not proven private gets a key-free branch, the public note and no item id in the PR title.

vars.description: Reusable string prefixes. ${name} in any config value (or a projects/*.md 'path:') expands to these, so a repo-root move is a one-line change.

backlogs.description: Backlog mirrors this instance tracks, one per space/project.

space.description: Space/project key (e.g. the tracker project id).

path.description: Backlog source — a per-item raw/ directory (post-migration) or a legacy backlog.json. ${var} expands.

memory.description: Configurable memory topology. Omit the whole block for the default: the instance's own memory/{raw,wiki,output} as the sole canon root plus vaults/* as federated mounts (byte-for-byte the prior behaviour). ${var} expands in paths. A broken/dangling path is skipped and reported, never fatal.

roots.description: Canon roots — counted AS the raw->wiki->output pipeline (promotable). Each declares a layout.

layout.description: flat = {raw,wiki,output} at the root. tier/project = {raw,wiki,output}/<project> — favours cross-project browsing on a directly-read root. project/tier = <project>/{raw,wiki,output} — favours per-project ownership and clean extraction, and is REQUIRED when the root is federated one-symlink-per-project (a project must map to a single mountable directory).

federated.description: Federated mounts — surfaced in the graph for navigation/context, NEVER counted as canon.
